description: Default Hermes lease shapes per actor type. Loaded by the gateway and Hermes /v1/hermes/action to mint a minimal lease for an actor whose request does not carry an explicit lease body. The 'allowed' lists hold canonical Hermes verbs (with adapter verbPrefix, e.g. 'cd.', 'desktop.', 'browser.') OR raw MCP tool names for servers without a verbPrefix. Risk ladder: read_only < low < medium < high < destructive < production. Hermes still runs all 8 LOOM gates regardless of what this file says — these are floors, not ceilings.
generated_for: Wave 3 — chrome-devtools + computer-use adapters on top of Wave 2 playwright

orangellm-fatty.description: OrangeLLM 'fatty' frontier-class model. Cheap-to-call reads + screenshot/UI observation. Cannot click, type, navigate, write files, deploy, or run code without lease elevation.
orangellm-fatty.notes: Fatty is the default chat-level reader. Screenshots and DOM/network reads are fine; any state-mutating verb requires lease elevation through Hermes.

orangellm-codexa.description: OrangeLLM 'codexa' execution model. Trusted to write code and navigate browsers/desktops to verify a change. Still cannot run arbitrary script, deploy, or delete.
orangellm-codexa.notes: Codexa can interact with browser/desktop UI to verify a fix, but file writes, file moves, and arbitrary script eval are still elevated. Inherits fatty's allow/forbid sets.

orangellm-coder.description: Code-writing actor. Same UI reach as codexa, plus filesystem writes inside the target project. No deploys, no destructive moves, no arbitrary SQL.
orangellm-coder.notes: Writes go through edit_file/write_file. Arbitrary code eval in a live page remains forbidden — that lane is operator-direct only.

operator-direct.description: Atom McCree direct keypress. Full reach short of destructive_write and production_deploy (those remain in global_forbidden and require an explicit override lease).
operator-direct.notes: Wildcard '*' is the only lease shape the adapter assertLeaseCoversVerb treats as 'any verb'. The global_forbidden list still blocks destructive_write / production_deploy / scope_expansion / egress_unbounded — operator-direct can NOT bypass those without minting an override lease with explicit forbidden=[].

operator-override.description: Operator-issued override lease for a single production / destructive operation. Short TTL, explicit allowed[], requires_approval=true so the gateway forces a confirm-step even though the operator is the one acting.
operator-override.notes: This shape is a template — the gateway must populate allowed[] with the specific verb(s) the operator is approving. Empty allowed[] means the lease grants nothing until the gateway fills it.

mission-runner.description: Background mission runner (codexa job, scheduled task). Read-heavy. Any UI action requires a per-mission lease, not this default.
mission-runner.notes: Missions that need to write or click must mint their own lease through the gateway. This default exists so a misconfigured mission cannot accidentally act — it can only observe.

unknown.description: Fail-closed default. Any actor type not in this file gets a lease that allows nothing.
unknown.notes: If you see leases minted with actor='unknown' in the audit log, the gateway is being called with an unrecognized actor — investigate before broadening this shape.
